posts.title: November 22 – Matthew 25
posts.description: THE SHEEP AND THE GOATS – Matthew 25:31-46 Why is the belief in heaven and hell waning, while the belief in reincarnation becomes more popular? Is this section more a parable or a prophecy? What does this section teach about Christian responsibility? How do people usually determine whether they will be nice to somebody? How would your behavior change if you treated each person in your life as if he or she were Jesus? In what way does this parable motivate you to tell your friends about Christ? How would you counter the idea that this passage teaches salvation by good works? What change does true faith make in a person’s life? In what specific ways has your faith in Christ changed you? Who are the needy people around you? What does this section tell us will hell will be like? (25:46) Is the judgment part consistent with what we believe about Jesus? posts.title: November 15 – Matthew 25
posts.description: THE PARABLE OF THE TALENTS – Matthew 25:14-30 Who were the most talented people you knew at school? What are some typical images people have of God? What would you do for God if you knew you could not fail at it? With what talents or resources has God entrusted you? Besides money or material possessions, what are some resources God has placed in our care? What thoughts or attitudes cause us to be lazy in carrying out our Christian responsibilities? What are the risks of investing our gifts for God’s service? What are the rewards of investing our gifts for God’s service? In what ways can you be a “good and faithful” servant? Where are you able to invest your gifts? What people can benefit most from the gifts and abilities you have? What discourages you from investing your talents? What encourages you to serve God with your talents? How would you grade yourself in your Christian stewardship over the last year? What resource do you need to commit to Christ’s use at this time in your life?

posts.title: November 8 – Matthew 25
posts.description: THE PARABLE OF THE TEN VIRGINS – Matthew 25:1-13 What is the most elaborate or important social function you have ever been invited to? If a meeting begins at 7:00pm, do you get there at 6:45? 7:05? Plan to leave your house at 7:00? Hope everyone else is late? When was a time you were late to an important event, and why were you delayed? In what ways do you tend to count on more mature Christians or try to ride their coattails? Who are you most like in this story? What responsibility does each Christian have before God? Why is continual preparation for Christ’s return better than “last minute cramming”? How do you feel about the door of the kingdom gets closed for some? Why do we tend to think (and act like) we have all the time in the world to get ready for Christ’s return? What does this passage say about the need for individual readiness? What are the possible consequences of putting off thinking about Christ and spiritual growth until later?
